title: Gor Mahia’s Kagame Cup Run Leaves Club With More to Prove
desc: Gor Mahia’s Kagame Cup run showed promise, but the final defeat to Rayon Sports raised fresh questions ahead of their next continental test
content:
Gor Mahia’s defeat in the CECAFA Kagame Cup final has left the Kenyan champions with both encouragement and unfinished business ahead of their next continental assignment.

K’Ogalo lost 2–1 to Rwanda’s Rayon Sports after extra time on Friday, ending their hopes of winning the regional title for the first time since 1985. The result means the club’s 41-year wait for another Kagame Cup crown will continue. 

The disappointment is significant because Gor Mahia had put together one of its strongest regional campaigns in years. The team topped its group, eliminated Al Hilal in a dramatic penalty shootout and reached the final for the first time since 2015. 

For supporters, the defeat will hurt because the trophy was within reach. Gor Mahia had recovered from an earlier group-stage loss to Vipers and showed the character needed to survive a tense semi-final, only to fall in extra time against the home side.

The campaign still gives coach Charles Akonnor valuable information before the CAF Champions League qualifiers. The technical bench must now examine the team’s finishing, game management and ability to maintain control when matches reach decisive moments. 

Chairman Ambrose Rachier has described the tournament run as impressive while also reflecting on the organisation of the competition. His assessment gives the club a chance to build on the progress rather than treat the final defeat as the whole story. 

What Gor Mahia does next will matter to more than its supporters. The club remains one of Kenya’s leading representatives in African football, and its performance will shape expectations for the country’s upcoming continental campaign.
